messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 2025-09-02T15:42:14Z prod-kv: high p99 latency + block-manager restarts detected. Auto-opened thread for paging/kv-cache regression. @oncall please triage.
emily: I'm on it. seeing alerts in Grafana. pinging SRE.
raj: digging in metrics now — heap_pages for block_manager spiked ~15:36 from ~2GB -> ~13.6GB. continuous-batcher queues also ballooned. Not normal.
maria: CS report: acme-inc and beta-shop started getting 502s/timeouts ~15:35 UTC. They say token generation stalled.
tyler: hypothesizing paged-kv metadata leak + small-block fragmentation. We have tons of tiny blocks (4K) and eviction isn't consolidating. That drives metadata size, which then causes eviction thrash.
emily: can we mitigate without full restart? what's low-risk hotfix?
raj: low-risk sequence: 1) reduce continuous batching concurrency 2) increase block size to force coalescing for new allocations 3) switch eviction to strict LRU to stop thrash 4) trigger targeted eviction of tiny blocks > threshold.
emily: do it. provide commands and I'll coordinate rollout.
tyler: hotfix commands (applied via infractl):
```
infractl apply --service prod-kv \ 
  --set continuous_batching.max_concurrency=8 \
  --set kv.block_manager.block_size=65536 \
  --set kv.eviction.policy=lru \
  --set kv.eviction.tiny_block_threshold=4096 \
  --set kv.eviction.force_evict=true
```
raj: applying in canary (bm-canary-01) now. will watch memory, evictions, and request latency.
ops-bot: rollout started for prod-kv: canary bm-canary-01 -> bm-canary-02. will pause on errors.
emily: monitoring: after patch, canary's heap_pages dropped 45% within 2 minutes. continuous-batcher queue reduced by ~70%. latency p99 improving.
maria: notifying impacted customers: short note to acme-inc and beta-shop that we're investigating, mitigation in progress, ETA ~30m. :white_check_mark:
cs-bot: Message sent to acme-inc (ticket #INC-4312) and beta-shop (ticket #INC-4313).
tyler: follow-up: we should also disable prefix/KV caching for long-tail keys for ~1hr to prevent cache churn. Command: `infractl set prod-kv kv.prefix_cache.enabled=false --duration 1h`
emily: applied that on canary and started rolling to 30% nodes. no regressions so far.
raj: note — logs show repeated failures in block_manager.MergeSmallBlocks: stack traces referencing `meta_index.append()` where metadata counter increases without corresponding release on error path. probable metadata leak in error branch.
tyler: ok we need a code rollback/patch. I'll open PR to add safe-decrement in the error path + unit test. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/7891 (WIP).
emily: operational doc updates: add alert when block_manager.metadata_size > 1GB or tiny_block_ratio > 0.25. Also add auto-toggle to backoff continuous batching if metadata growth detected.
maria: customer impact summary (so far): acme-inc saw ~120 failed requests over 20m, beta-shop ~40 failures. No data loss. Some increased latencies for a broader set of customers but degraded rather than complete outage.
tyler: after canary success, rolling to remaining bm nodes with 10% step increments. ops-bot: proceeding.
ops-bot: rolling update at 15:59 UTC: 10% -> 20% -> 40% -> 70% -> 100%. No rollback triggered.
emily: confirmed overall cluster heap_pages down ~50% vs peak. p99 latency returning to baseline.
raj: long-term actions: (A) patch metadata leak (PR 7891), (B) add block-manager GC compaction pass to merge small blocks periodically, (C) add integration tests that simulate eviction thrash and ensure metadata counters stable, (D) add a throttling guard in continuous-batcher that checks metadata headroom.
maria: CS follow-ups: send postmortem + timeline to impacted customers and offer dedicated sync if they want.
tyler: quick mitigation notes for runbook: include commands above + a `force-evict` script: 
```
# evict tiny blocks older than 1h
kvtool evict --service prod-kv --older-than 1h --max-block-size 4096 --dry-run=false
```
emily: handoff: I'm continuing as primary oncall until 03:00 UTC. raj will be secondary and will own follow-up tickets.
raj: acknowledged. I'll pick up the PR reviews and follow-ups tomorrow morning.
emily: incident severity: Sev2 (customer impact but mitigated quickly). Postmortem owner: tyler. ETA for postmortem draft: 2025-09-04.
maria: noted. I'll coordinate customer comms after postmortem draft.
incident-bot: Incident closed to active mitigation channel at 17:01:02Z. Please file follow-ups and tag #postmortems.
